exam.title: Professional Machine Learning Engineer
exam.study_prerequisites: No formal prerequisite; Google recommends three or more years of industry experience including one year on Google Cloud. Practice Python/SQL interpretation, governed features/data, predictive and generative model selection/evaluation, reproducible experiments/training, accelerator choices, registry/batch/online serving, canary/A-B rollout, pipeline CI/CD/CT, drift/skew/safety/security monitoring and rollback.

objective_coverage.objective_group: Collaborating within and across teams to manage data and models (~16%)

review.notes: All six June 1, 2026 domains are mapped across predictive and generative AI through task/data/model choice, collaboration/lineage, reproducible training/accelerators, serving/rollout, pipelines/CI-CD-CT and continuous quality/safety/security/cost operation. Three scenarios, eight labs and 36 checks are included. All eight URLs are cataloged: seven reachable and O'Reilly automation-blocked. The different older PDF is explicitly rejected as the current baseline.

findings.title: Missing monitored validity does not mean indefinite certification
Prediction inputs follow the stored transformation contract
Latest online features do not reconstruct historical training
Latest null can retain older non-null values
Repeated evaluation can contaminate held-out evidence
Aggregate metrics and unsupported ratios conceal failures
Connectivity and readiness have different failure actions
Online and batch scaling contracts differ
A reused pipeline result has no automatic expiry
Model Monitoring v2 is not a universal real-time AI monitor
External reference monitoring has model and attribution limits
Scheduled monitoring still executes batch jobs
